title: Getting Help
description: Explain symptoms, ask for help, and agree on an appropriate next action.
objectives: Explain symptoms, ask for help, and agree on an appropriate next action.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to explain symptoms, ask for help, and agree on an appropriate next action. The central language is integrated symptom, advice, and conditional review. It belongs to the practical context of health & everyday problems. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: integrated symptom, advice, and conditional review

blocks.english: I've had a headache since this morning.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the getting help exchange.

blocks.english: If it gets worse, I'll visit urgent care.
blocks.explanation: This getting help model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the getting help exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I've had a headache since this morning.” and “If it gets worse, I'll visit urgent care.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: integrated symptom, advice, and conditional review.
